linked_inci_ids: ING-030 (Sodium Lauroyl Methyl Isethionate), ING-032 (Sodium Methyl Oleoyl Taurate), ING-034 (Coco-Glucoside)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Mild plant-derived cleansers that lift sweat, dirt, and light buildup while leaving hair soft, detanglable, and hydrated.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Ideal for weekly wash days across all porosities, including dry, color-treated, or fragile hair.

linked_inci_ids: ING-031 (Cocamidopropyl Betaine), ING-116 (Cocamidopropyl Hydroxysultaine), ING-035 (PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Not the main cleaner. They boost foam, thicken the shampoo, and soften the feel of a stronger cleanser, or put some softness back during the wash.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Look for them right after the main cleanser. They help a blend feel gentler, but they do not make a strong cleanser mild on their own.

how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Not a sulfate, but a high-detergency cleanser that lifts oil, product, and residue fast. "Sulfate-free" does not mean gentle.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Good for occasional clarifying, oily scalps, or heavy styling-product buildup. On dry, tightly coiled, or high-porosity hair, look for a milder cleanser first, and follow with a deep conditioner.

linked_inci_ids: ING-083 (Sodium Lauryl Sulfate) and ING-084 (Sodium Laureth Sulfate).
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Strong negatively charged cleansers that strip heavy oils, silicones, waxes, and scalp buildup fast.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Best reserved for periodic clarifying or stubborn buildup—too stripping for weekly wash days on dry 3C–4C coils.

linked_inci_ids: ING-113 (Disodium/Tetrasodium EDTA), ING-114 (Sodium Phytate), ING-021 (Citric Acid), ING-020 (Tartaric Acid), ING-096 (Gluconolactone)
how_it_behaves_on_coily_hair: Bind calcium, magnesium, and metal ions from hard water so they rinse away instead of interfering with washing. They are not foaming detergents.
porosity_and_wash_out_guidance: Useful if you have hard water, swim, or find products stop working even after clarifying. Strength differs by ingredient, so a chelator in a formula does not guarantee every mineral deposit is removed.
